documents.title: Sai Krishna Vala — approved professional overview
documents.text: I am Sai Krishna Vala. I have around five years of Dynamics 365 and Power Platform experience across Sales, Customer Service, Field Service and Power Pages. I started with requirements analysis and moved into hands-on development. I have built plugins, Power Automate flows, business process flows and business rules. I work with stakeholders, clients and development teams, and have led projects involving integrations, AI chat experiences and dashboards. I have a master’s degree in Computer Science from Saint Leo University.

documents.title: Target roles
documents.text: I am interested in Dynamics 365 Developer, Power Platform Developer, Technical Consultant, Functional Consultant and Team Lead roles.

documents.title: 4A Consulting — team leadership and product ownership
documents.text: At 4A Consulting, I am a team lead across four applications using Power Apps and Dynamics CRM. I coordinate work across the sales and hiring domains. I take on product ownership responsibilities by translating stakeholder requirements into technical work.

documents.title: 4A Consulting — engineering work
documents.text: At 4A Consulting, I built the core Field Service domain and Power Pages experiences. I also built Power Automate flows, C# plugins and PCF controls.

documents.title: Lululemon — collaborative Dynamics work
documents.text: At Lululemon, I worked with the team on Sales and co-built Customer Service, Power Pages and Field Service solutions. This was collaborative work; I do not describe those solutions as work I built entirely alone.

documents.title: Lululemon — connected customer service experience
documents.text: I co-built a connected service experience with the Lululemon team. Customers sign in to Power Pages, view relevant products and create service requests. Requests become Customer Service cases. When a visit is needed, Field Service supports scheduling and technician assignment. Customers receive a satisfaction survey after service, feedback is recorded in Customer Service, and service information supports sales follow-up actions and sequences.

documents.title: Plugin — stage validation and task generation
documents.text: I built plugins that validate required data and authorization before a stage transition. The transition stops when checks fail. The plugins create related stage records, generate tasks from templates, calculate due dates, and assign tasks to owners or teams.

documents.title: PCF — model-driven controls
documents.text: I built a React-based dashboard PCF control inside a model-driven form for a sales team. I also built form-field, dataset or view, and custom-page PCF controls. The custom-page example is inside a model-driven app, not a standalone canvas app.

documents.title: Task and calendar automation
documents.text: For task and calendar automation, templates are maintained in Dynamics. Power Automate and Microsoft Graph support notifications and Outlook integration. When a task is completed, the flow deletes its associated Outlook calendar event. A plugin deactivates the corresponding calendar record inside the application. The completed task and application calendar history are preserved; this does not delete a Planner task.

documents.title: Business problem and consulting approach
documents.text: The business needed a more connected way to manage sales, customer service and finance-related processes. My focus was understanding requirements and translating them into CRM functionality, connecting business records and adapting Dynamics 365 so users could capture information, follow the right process and work with relevant data. Finance-related context is confirmed only at this general level; specific Finance and Operations modules remain unconfirmed.

documents.title: Personal customization and wider-team ownership
documents.text: I personally customized Dynamics 365 Sales, Customer Service and Power Pages to support business requirements. I worked with the wider team, which built the overall enterprise solution, including Power Automate workflows and other business automation. My responsibility was to make my customizations fit the broader process rather than treating each application as isolated.

documents.title: Approach to a new CRM requirement
documents.text: I start by understanding the business process, users, information needs and decisions the system must support. I assess standard Dynamics 365 capabilities before custom development. When an extension is needed, I use plugins for server-side logic, PCF for richer interactions and Power Automate for workflow coordination. I consider connected modules, access, data quality, testing and deployment.

documents.title: Testing approach
documents.text: I test the complete business journey, including successful actions and conditions that should stop the process. For stage-management logic, I check required information, authorization, record creation, task assignment and due dates. For integrations, I check intended connected-system results. I work with the team and business users to confirm the solution meets the requirement before release. This does not establish a specific deployment pipeline, rollback procedure or automated coverage percentage.

documents.title: Qualitative solution improvements
documents.text: The solution connected previously separate activities into a business process. Customers could initiate service through the portal, internal teams could manage the case and field work, and feedback could return to the service process. Stage and task automation added validation, ownership and due dates. These are qualitative functional improvements, not numerical time savings, adoption figures, revenue results or measured performance gains.

documents.title: Portfolio confidentiality approach
documents.text: In this portfolio, I explain the business problem, my contribution, the technical approach and approved outcomes. I use illustrative workflows without exposing production records, credentials, customer information or confidential implementation details. If information is outside approved public knowledge, I direct visitors to contact me. This is my portfolio disclosure policy, not an employer policy.
